summary: Security-audit iteration: verified slowapi rate limits, Pydantic length caps, generic 500 message; ran full backend regression + frontend smoke. All 26 backend pytest tests pass (100%). Frontend Library (3 categories), dialect filters, Prompt Generator (idea->result->copy), and Contact form (submit + success) all work correctly.
critical_code_review_comments: Rate-limit test via public URL initially returned 200x7 because ingress/load-balancer surfaces different client IPs to slowapi's get_remote_address. Verified via localhost:8001 that 5/min contact limit correctly returns 429. Consider enabling ProxyHeadersMiddleware / forwarded_allow_ips so per-user rate limiting works reliably behind the ingress (currently effective limit at ingress may not match per-user intent).
server.py uses deprecated @app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown'); switch to lifespan handlers for FastAPI >=0.109.
CORS allow_origins defaults to '*' with allow_credentials=True — invalid combo per CORS spec; should whitelist explicit origins in prod.
seed_data_creation: None. Contact form submissions prefixed TEST_ inserted during tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Rate limit tests must hit localhost:8001 to bypass ingress IP shuffling; if using public URL, expect 200s only. Wait 60s between rate-limit bursts. All 26 pytests green (test_backend.py + test_security.py). LLM calls average 5-25s so keep timeouts >=45s.
rca of the issue: Initial rate-limit test failure was NOT an app bug: through the public Kubernetes ingress, requests are distributed across pods / present with proxy source IPs, so slowapi's per-IP counter never accumulates 5 within a minute. Verified feature works correctly by hitting the pod-local endpoint (http://localhost:8001) — 200x5 then 429. Fix in test: point rate-limit test at localhost.
